title: Polyglot API ergonomics checklist and quicklabs
content:
Purpose:

Capture a compact, pragmatic checklist for API ergonomics we want across Redwood SDKs (JS/Python/Go/Java), plus 3 short instructor-led quicklabs (30m each) that can be used in onboarding sessions and office hours. This is intentionally implementation-agnostic but practical: the checklist will drive concrete API shapes, examples, and testcases.

Audience:
- SDK engineers (authors and maintainers)
- Developer advocates running workshops
- Solutions engineers building quickstarts for customers

Scope:
- Client surface design (constructor, auth, default options)
- Runtime ergonomics (sync/async, streaming primitives, cancellation)
- Errors and retries (shape, telemetry, user-recoverable vs internal)
- Examples & quicklabs that demonstrate common patterns: chat+tools, embeddings+search, streaming generation

High-level problems we observe:
- Inconsistent async primitives across languages -> cognitive load for polyglot users
- Too many optional defaults -> onboarding friction and accidental misconfigurations
- Streaming / chunked APIs are different shape per SDK and rarely tested end-to-end in onboarding labs
- Error surface differs (exceptions vs rich error objects) which makes instrumentation and docs tricky

Principles (opinionated):
1) Keep first-run path tiny: 3 lines to do something useful (instantiate client, call chat/generate, print).
2) Make streaming first-class: offer the same conceptual primitive (iterator/async iterator/callback) in each language with mapped ergonomics.
3) Telemetry hooks: easy place to attach request id, per-call metadata, and token-level timing.
4) Fail loud but helpful: explicit error object with stable codes + human_message when available.
5) Single canonical example per feature (chat, embed, rerank, stream) and do not duplicate slightly different variants across docs.

Ergonomics checklist (concrete):
- Client construction:
  - Single main entrypoint named Client (or RedwoodClient) in each SDK.
  - Accepts (apiKey, region, options) with env fallback and clear error message when missing.
  - Minimal default retry/backoff policy; opt-in to aggressive batching.
- Method surface:
  - Methods aligned to API verbs: generate(), chat(), embed(), rerank().
  - Synchronous wrappers for simple blocking use-cases where language idioms expect it (e.g., blocking call in Go, sync call in Python for quick scripts).
  - Async-first implementations with explicit sync adaptors documented.
- Streaming:
  - Streaming results exposed as:
    - JS: AsyncIterable of events, with a small helper to aggregate text.
    - Python: AsyncIterator + sync generator wrapper.
    - Go: Channel-based stream + Cancel context integration.
  - Include sample code to resume after partial failures using request_id + resume_cursor.
- Responses & typing:
  - Typed response object with: id, model, tokens_consumed (number), warnings (list), meta (dict/Map), content variants.
  - Provide easy serialisation helpers (to_json, from_json) for logging.
- Errors:
  - Unified Error class (RedwoodError) with fields: code, message, hint, request_id.
  - Mapped to native language exceptions but preserve fields for telemetry.
- Retries & idempotency:
  - Retry-once default for transient network failures; expose retry config on client and per-call.
  - Idempotency-key optional param for non-idempotent calls (generate) with clear semantics.
- Telemetry integration:
  - Hook/callback that receives per-request timing and token-level events.
  - Minimal example that wires to console logging and to our datadog/otel SDKs.
- Documentation & examples:
  - One canonical Quickstart per language with a single sample app (chat + embed search).
  - Copy-pasteable snippets under 10 lines for first-run.
- Testing & CI:
  - End-to-end smoke tests that run a streaming scenario in each language on CI (recorded fixtures for determinism).

Quicklabs (30 minutes each) - instructor notes + expected outcomes:

Lab A - "Hello chat + tool calling" (30m)\- Objective: Get a simple chat agent running that calls a mocked tool (calendar) when prompted.
- Pre-reqs: Node 18 or Python 3.11 installed, API key env var (REDWOOD_API_KEY).
- Steps:
  1) Install SDK (npm i @redwood/sdk) or (pip install redwood-sdk).
  2) Instantiate client with env fallback.
  3) Call chat() with a system prompt and a user prompt that triggers a tool.
  4) Wire a simple tool callback that returns structured JSON; show function-calling signature.
  5) Observe streaming tokens and final structured output.
- Instructor tips: show both streaming aggregation and direct final payload. Demonstrate how to capture request_id and look it up in Console.
- Outcome: Participant can run chat with function-calling and see telemetry request_id.

Lab B - "Embeddings -> similarity search -> rerank" (30m)\- Objective: Build a tiny pipeline that embeds a small corpus, runs a similarity lookup for a user query, then reranks top-k using a rerank API call.
- Steps:
  1) Create 10 tiny docs (local JSON file).
  2) Call embed() for each doc and store vectors in memory (or use simple sqlite).
  3) Implement cosine similarity function (helper snippet provided).
  4) For the top 3 hits, call rerank() (or call generate() with combined context) to pick the best answer.
- Instructor tips: emphasize vector dimensions and how to interpret token costs shown in Console.
- Outcome: Participant ships a 50-line script that returns a coherent answer from local docs.

Lab C - "Streaming generator + cancellation + resume" (30m)\- Objective: Show how a long generation can be cancelled and resumed with a resume_cursor.
- Steps:
  1) Start a streaming generate() that yields tokens every 100ms (server sim).
  2) Cancel from the client after N tokens; show graceful cleanup.
  3) Resume using a stored resume_cursor (or use prefix caching) to continue generation.
- Notes: demonstrate race conditions and best-practice state management for UIs.
- Outcome: Participant understands cancellation semantics, resume token, and how KV prefix caching reduces cost.

Example snippets (JS-style pseudo):
- Minimal first-run (30s):
  import RedwoodClient from '@redwood/sdk'
  const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
  const r = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-2', prompt: 'Write a haiku about coffee' })
  console.log(r.content[0].text)

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Decide on exact method names for language idiomaticity (generate vs completions). Ticket: JIRA-RDW-1409
- Agree on error code taxonomy and mapping to HTTP 4xx/5xx. Refer to Confluence page above.
- Determine whether to expose idempotency-key by default on client or per-call.
- Prototype a tiny adapter package that wraps async iterators into Node streams for ecosystem compatibility.

Rollout plan (high level):
1) Sync with each SDK owner on checklist and adapt language idioms (2 weeks).
2) Implement streaming helpers and a canonical Quickstart repo (3 weeks).
3) Add CI smoke tests and workshop materials (1 week).
4) Schedule internal brown-bag and record short 10m walkthrough videos (1 week).

Acceptance criteria for merging SDK changes:
- First-run script runs in <30s environment bootstrap (fresh VM)
- Streaming sample passed in CI with recorded fixtures
- Telemetry hook present and example shows request_id in Console
- Docs updated with one canonical snippet per feature and copy-pasteable code block

Meeting notes (2024-11-05 internal discussion):
- Diego: wants consistent error shape across SDKs; push error.code mandatory.
- Sophie: streaming ergonomics are high priority for mobile teams.
- Marcus: telemetry needs to expose per-token timing without leaking sensitive content.

Links for implementation:
- github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-templates (starter templates)
- github.com/redwood-inference/quickstarts (example apps used in labs)
- JIRA: RDW-1342, RDW-1409, RDW-1501

Notes to self (scratch):
- Keep workshop labs under 300 lines each.
- Record audio notes for lab run-throughs and attach to Confluence.
- Add a small checklist for customer-facing SDKs to verify compliance with SSO and KMS patterns.

If you're reading this and want to run a quicklab in a session: copy the lab folder from github.com/redwood-inference/quickstarts/polyglot-labs and follow the README. Ping #dev-ex on slack for help.
